headline: Brigham nurses authorize open-ended strike as contract talks stall
dek: About 4,000 nurses voted 93% to give their union authority to call an indefinite walkout, but no strike date has been set.
body: About 4,000 nurses at Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston voted 2,986 to 215 on Sept. 24 to authorize an open-ended strike, the Massachusetts Nurses Association said. The 93% vote gives the union’s bargaining committee authority to call an indefinite walkout if negotiations with Mass General Brigham do not produce a contract.

The authorization does not itself start a strike. The union has not announced a date, and nurses would have to provide at least 10 days’ notice before walking out. GBH News reported that the vote follows a one-day strike at the hospital in July and a four-day lockout that ended when nurses returned to work.

The nurses’ union says the dispute includes compensation, health-insurance costs, permanent staffing and the hospital system’s reliance on temporary nurses. Mass General Brigham told GBH it has bargained in good faith and says its proposal preserves the 20-step wage scale, continued increases for nurses moving through the scale and additional increases or bonuses for nurses at the top step.

MGB also said a strike is a decision only the union can make and that it has plans to continue providing care if one is called. The Brigham vote comes a week after Boston Medical Center nurses authorized a possible three-day strike, adding to labor pressure at major Boston hospitals.

For now, the Brigham result is a strike authorization rather than a scheduled walkout. The next concrete milestone will be whether negotiators return to the table or the union issues the required notice.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: Brigham and Women’s nurses authorized an open-ended strike, but no walkout date has been set as contract talks with Mass General Brigham continue.
